title: Increased TSPO alleviates neuropathic pain by preventing pyroptosis via the AMPK-PGC-1alpha pathway.
authors: Li, Baolong; Yu, Kaiming; Zhou, Xiongyao; Sun, Jialu; Qi, Le; Li, Weiye; Yang, Tuo; Li, Weizhen; Wang, Ningning; Gu, Xiaosong; Cui, Shusen; Cao, Rangjuan
journal: The journal of headache and pain
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨TSPO通过AMPK-PGC-1alpha通路缓解神经病理性疼痛，核心为疼痛机制与线粒体功能，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Neuropathic pain poses a significant clinical challenge, largely due to the incomplete understanding of its molecular mechanisms, particularly the role of mitochondrial dysfunction. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that pyroptosis and inflammatory responses induced by spared nerve injury (SNI) in the spinal dorsal horn play a critical role in the initiation and persistence of neuropathic pain. Among the factors involved, TSPO (translocator protein) emerged as a key regulator. Our experimental findings showed that TSPO expression was upregulated during neuropathic pain, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, specifically manifested as impaired mitochondrial biogenesis, disrupted mitochondrial dynamics (including insufficient expression of mitochondrial biogenesis and fusion-related proteins, as well as significantly increased expression of fission-related proteins), and activation of pyroptosis. Pharmacological upregulation of TSPO, but not its downregulation, effectively alleviated SNI-induced pain hypersensitivity, improving mitochondrial function and reducing pyroptosis. Immunofluorescence staining confirmed that TSPO was primarily localized in astrocytes, and its expression mirrored the protective effects on mitochondrial health and pyroptosis prevention. PCR array analysis suggested a strong association between TSPO and the mitochondrial regulation pathway AMPK-PGC-1alpha. Notably, inhibition of AMPK-PGC-1alpha abolished TSPO effects on mitochondrial balance and pyroptosis suppression. Furthermore, Mendelian randomization analysis of GWAS data indicated that increased TSPO expression was linked to pain relief. Through drug screening, molecular docking, and behavioral assays, we identified zopiclone as a promising TSPO-targeting drug for pain treatment. In summary, this study enhances our understanding of the molecular interplay between TSPO, mitochondrial health, and neuropathic pain, highlighting TSPO as a potential therapeutic target for pain management.
abstract_zh: 神经病理性疼痛构成重大临床挑战，主要归因于对其分子机制的不完全理解，尤其是线粒体功能障碍的作用。生物信息学分析揭示， spared nerve injury (SNI) 诱导的脊髓背角焦亡 (pyroptosis) 和炎症反应在神经病理性疼痛的发生和持续中发挥关键作用。在所涉及的因素中，TSPO (translocator protein) 被确定为核心调控因子。我们的实验结果显示，TSPO 表达在神经病理性疼痛期间上调，伴随线粒体功能障碍，具体表现为线粒体生物合成受损、线粒体动力学紊乱（包括线粒体生物合成和融合相关蛋白表达不足，以及分裂相关蛋白表达显著增加），以及焦亡激活。药理学上调 TSPO，而非下调，有效缓解了 SNI 诱导的疼痛超敏反应，改善了线粒体功能并减少了焦亡。免疫荧光染色证实，TSPO 主要定位于星形胶质细胞，其表达反映了对线粒体健康和焦亡预防的保护效应。PCR 阵列分析提示，TSPO 与线粒体调控通路 AMPK-PGC-1alpha 之间存在强关联。值得注意的是，抑制 AMPK-PGC-1alpha 消除了 TSPO 对线粒体平衡和焦亡抑制的作用。此外，对 GWAS 数据的孟德尔随机化分析表明，TSPO 表达增加与疼痛缓解相关。通过药物筛选、分子对接和行为学实验，我们鉴定出佐匹克隆 (zopiclone) 作为靶向 TSPO 的潜在疼痛治疗药物。总之，本研究增进了我们对 TSPO、线粒体健康与神经病理性疼痛之间分子相互作用的理解，强调 TSPO 是疼痛管理的潜在治疗靶点。
